style.vernacular: Atlantic peninsula capital with a French colonial Plateau of 3-6 storey rendered blocks in cream, ochre and faded pink with louvred shutters and balconies, 1930s Art Deco and Neo-Sudanese civic buildings, 1960s Senghor-era modernist concrete, and a dense Medina of 2-4 storey painted concrete houses and shops with flat roofs and rebar sticking out. Hot semi-arid with Atlantic sea breeze; sandy ground, palms, baobabs and neem; many buildings are repainted in bright blues, greens and yellows.
style.ornament: Neo-Sudanese towers and Byzantine domes on 1930s landmarks; Moroccan-style tilework and arches on the Grand Mosque; louvred shutters and wrought balconies on colonial blocks; green, white and red tile accents on Mouride and Layene mosques; bright murals and hand-painted shop signs in the Medina.

sources.what: BSh hot semi-arid climate; Plateau as European colonial district, Medina as African quarter; presidential palace 1907; Dakar station 1885; Mamelles lighthouse 1864; laterite blocks used in 1795 walls; Grand Mosque 1964 and Mosque of the Divinity 1973
